definition: An area of the Shelf or lower Old Harbor that has been slowly buried under layers of infrastructure — new piping, cable runs, temporary structures made permanent — until the original architecture is unrecognizable. Residents of silt neighborhoods often have no official address.
origin: Geographic slang coined by urban surveyors, adopted by residents as a term of grim pride.
usage: Used by Shelf residents, city planners, and journalists covering displacement.
example: My grandmother's building is in a silt neighborhood so deep even Ferrogate doesn't bother patrolling — they'd need a map from 2140.
